title: Market women’s peace and electoral-inclusion march in Cotonou, 31 October 2020
location: Cotonou, with starting-point disagreement between reports (near SOGEMA versus the Dantokpa market triangle); other sources list activity in other communes but do not provide a per-site attendance count. Parakou is represented separately in BEN202010_E002.
organizer: Organizer naming differs across sources: Bénin Web TV names the Mouvement des Femmes Béninoises pour la Paix, while Front Souverain’s call names the Mouvement des Femmes Leader du Bénin pour la Paix; equivalence is unresolved. La Nouvelle Tribune reports opposition-personality support.
threshold_50_evidence: Neither opened report gives attendance estimates or per-site counts; the ≥50 simultaneous-participant threshold is not established.

start_date.summary: Both sources date the women’s march to 31 October 2020.

location.summary: Sources give differing Cotonou starting points (near SOGEMA vs Dantokpa market triangle) and a list of several communes; exact relation between locations/marches is unresolved.

demands.summary: Reports concern political peace, fundamental freedoms, rule of law and inclusive presidential election process in Benin.

participants.summary: No qualifying numeric count or simultaneous site-level threshold evidence found.

occurrence.summary: Two opened local outlets report an executed march; source independence and underlying organizer materials remain unresolved.

organizer.summary: The women’s peace movement is named; opposition-personality support is reported.

notes: Cotonou site-level candidate only. Reports of other communes are not aggregated into this record; organizer-name variants and route details remain unresolved.
open_questions: Resolve Cotonou route and exact demand recipient.
Find independent Cotonou participant estimate; do not aggregate counts across towns.
Clarify municipal ban exception and actual enforcement.

title: Women’s peace/electoral-inclusion march in Parakou, 31 October 2020
location: Parakou: Daabaaru reports a route from the municipal stadium to Place Tabéra, where organizers read a declaration. Le Parakois’ search-result excerpt describes a separate/possibly same route starting near a literacy hall and says police accompanied participants; relationship between descriptions is unresolved.
organizer: Daabaaru names Femmes Leaders Engagées pour la Paix au Bénin, led by Marie-Reine Yankpè. Le Parakois’ search-only header/excerpt says local women; organizer equivalence is unknown.
threshold_50_evidence: Le Parakois search-only excerpt reports about 100 participants, but its exact page returned a tool-level error and this figure is not body-verified; Daabaaru gives no count. ≥50 simultaneous participants remains pending.

occurrence.summary: Daabaaru’s opened local report describes a Parakou march on 31 Oct and receipt of its declaration by a municipal secretary. The Le Parakois search-only excerpt reports roughly 100 people, but the exact page did not load; do not treat that snippet as verified attendance.

participants.summary: No qualifying simultaneous count at this site.

start_date.summary: Daabaaru dates the Parakou march to 31 October 2020.

location.summary: Daabaaru gives the route stadium to Place Tabéra; the search-only Le Parakois excerpt gives a literacy hall start and city route. Relationship is unresolved.

organizer.summary: Daabaaru identifies Femmes Leaders Engagées pour la Paix au Bénin and its president Marie-Reine Yankpè.

demands.summary: Declaration reportedly called for democratic restoration and inclusive/equitable elections.

notes: Candidate retained for review; no threshold aggregation across sites or dates.
open_questions: Find independent per-site attendance evidence and clarify episode scope.
